checks_by_claim.claim: Wrong interchange between rho cofiber and slices
checks_by_claim.source_location: PDF p.8 proof of Theorem 3.1; conventions pp.3,6
checks_by_claim.verification: Exactness does not remove the Tate shift: the correct fixed-q triangle is Sigma^(-1,-1) s_(q+1)Y -> s_qY -> s_q(C(rho) tensor Y). The printed ordinary-cofiber identity ignores this slice reindexing.

checks_by_claim.claim: Admissible witness for the general identity, with exact counterexample scope
checks_by_claim.verification: Over Q let H=HF2 be cellular and pure slice zero, and X=C(rho) tensor H. Its only slices are s0X=H and s_-1X=Sigma^(0,-1)H, so its tower is finite/convergent; real Betti realization vanishes. Since 2 acts trivially, Y=X/2 splits as X plus Sigma^(1,0)X. Hence s0(C(rho) tensor Y)=H plus Sigma^(1,0)H. Its rho-localization is nonzero: the ordered-field Milnor K sign map sends powers of {-1} to nonzero powers of t. In contrast, the localization of any ordinary C(rho) tensor object is zero.
checks_by_claim.counterexample_scope: The witness does not have zero algebraic-closure pullback, so it is not a counterexample satisfying every kernel assumption of Theorem 3.1. It refutes the general identity invoked as a proof step.
checks_by_claim.severity_reason: That false identity is the necessary bridge used to apply Proposition 3.8 in the core conservativity reduction. The repair does not reduce this proof defect's Major severity.

checks_by_claim.verification: Let Y=C(rho) tensor X/2 and N_q=s_qY over the original base. After the specified cellular base changes, each pure q-slice M_q is an HF2-module and has zero algebraic-closure pullback. Proposition 3.8 applied to C(rho) tensor M_q gives zero. Thus rho acts invertibly and M_q is isomorphic to Sigma^(1,1)M_q. It is both (q+1)-effective and in the right orthogonal to that subcategory, so M_q=0. Field detection then gives N_q=0 globally. The assumed global slice convergence, preserved by the finite cofibers and Tate shifts used here, gives Y=0; Lemma 3.4 and the stated 2-torsion condition complete the restricted repair.
checks_by_claim.external_hypotheses: RSO Corollary 2.17 requires connected bases, compatible pairs and cellular spectra. These hypotheses and the required invertibility of residue characteristics are retained, not replaced by an unconditional base-change claim.
checks_by_claim.limit: External motivic theorems are used with their verified stated hypotheses; no new proof of all their foundations or commutation with arbitrary infinite completion is claimed.

checks_by_claim.source_location: Source Section 4; GIKR published pp.14–17, Proposition 3.26 and Lemma 3.25
checks_by_claim.verification: The cited tensor-comparison theorem requires the first spectrum to be bounded below, finite type and even-cell. Periodic KU is not bounded below. The nearby sequential-colimit theorem also requires uniform boundedness below and connectivity tending to infinity. No verified extension removing these hypotheses was supplied.
checks_by_claim.disposition: Keep as an unverified external dependency/repair limitation. Do not claim the intended KU comparison is false or create a second confirmed Major without a decisive counterexample.
